executive_summary.text: Critical PHP RCE flaws tracked as PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) are under mass exploitation, with Amazon detecting attempts four days before patches shipped and Mirai botnet operators now joining in with ASLR-bypass exploits.

China-nexus actor Storm-0940 weaponized the ARTEX agentic AI framework in its ConnectWise Cloud Backup supply chain compromise, automating credential abuse against more than 2,250 Microsoft 365 tenants.

LiteLLM's release pipeline was hijacked for the second supply chain compromise of 2026, with a leaked master key enabling attackers to steal GitHub CLI OAuth tokens and push info-stealer malware via PyPI and Docker releases.

A third Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator zero-day in four months, a critical SQL injection (CVE-2026-114625) that escalates read-only customer credentials to operator level, is actively exploited and now on the CISA KEV catalog.

Certificate authority eMudhra is exiting the global TLS business after eight intermediate CA private keys were found trivially guessable, including one that was simply '4', a trust-chain compromise that enables rogue certificate signing and MitM traffic interception.

cyber_news.title: BlackX UEFI bootkit bypasses Secure Boot via Baton Drop flaw in espionage campaign against Central Asian diplomatic targets
cyber_news.summary: A new UEFI bootkit named BlackX was deployed in an early-2026 espionage campaign against diplomatic entities in Central Asia. The bootkit exploits the older Baton Drop vulnerability to bypass Secure Boot and loads a malicious driver that interferes with Kaspersky and Avast security products.
cyber_news.expanded: BlackX abuses the Baton Drop flaw in the Windows boot manager to defeat Secure Boot protections and install a kernel-mode driver early in the boot sequence. The malicious driver is specifically engineered to neutralize security agents from Kaspersky and Avast by tampering with their driver components before they fully initialize. Notably, the bootkit remains effective even on fully patched Windows systems where SBAT revocation updates have not been applied, since the underlying boot manager vulnerability persists without those firmware-level revocations. The campaign's targeting of diplomatic missions in Central Asia is consistent with state-aligned espionage collection rather than financially motivated crime.

cyber_news.title: Widespread token-spraying attacks target Microsoft 365 accounts for BEC and email compromise
cyber_news.summary: Attackers are running broad token-spraying campaigns against Microsoft 365 accounts, replaying stolen authentication tokens to establish sessions and pivot into business email compromise. The activity blends phishing, stolen session tokens, and social engineering against help desks.
cyber_news.expanded: Rather than password spraying, the actors spray stolen or fraudulently obtained tokens (including OAuth refresh tokens and session cookies) against Microsoft 365 authentication endpoints. Because the tokens are replayed directly, password-based MFA is sidestepped entirely and the session appears legitimate to services that trust the issued token. Where token replay fails, the operators fall back to help-desk social engineering to trigger MFA resets or credential changes on targeted accounts. The end goal is mailbox access for BEC: inbox rule creation, payment-fraud lures, and lateral movement into partner communications.

cyber_news.title: Brotli decoder flaw (CVE-2026-111497) behind Node.js RCE also affects Bun, Python, and Envoy; Node2Shell PoC demonstrated
cyber_news.summary: A memory-corruption flaw in the Brotli decompression library that enables RCE in Node.js also affects Bun, Python's Brotli and brotlicffi bindings, and Envoy proxy. Researchers have published a working Node2Shell proof of concept demonstrating full remote code execution.
cyber_news.expanded: The vulnerability is a memory-corruption bug in the Brotli decoder that triggers when decompressing specially crafted compressed data, making any service that decompresses attacker-controlled Brotli streams externally reachable. Node.js shipped fixes across all supported lines (22.x, 24.x, and 26.x) on October 21, but the shared upstream library means Bun, Python's Brotli and brotlicffi packages, and Envoy inherit the same decoder defect until each project pulls the patched code. The public Node2Shell PoC demonstrates a complete exploit chain from crafted compressed payload to shell execution, significantly lowering the barrier for opportunistic exploitation of unpatched runtimes.

cyber_news.title: Campaign breaches enterprise firewalls and VPN edge devices, exposing 70,000+ credentials
cyber_news.summary: An ongoing campaign has compromised enterprise edge devices including FortiGate firewalls and Palo Alto GlobalProtect VPN appliances, harvesting more than 70,000 credentials. Operators are following up with active compromise attempts against the exposed environments.
cyber_news.expanded: The campaign focuses on internet-facing network edge appliances, exploiting weak or default administrative credentials and unpatched firmware on FortiGate and GlobalProtect deployments to establish footholds. Once inside, the actors extract configuration data and stored credential material, including VPN accounts and potentially password stores, amassing a pool of 70,000+ credentials. The harvested credentials are then used for follow-on intrusion attempts, including attempts to authenticate into the corporate networks behind the breached edge devices. The scale and appliance focus mirror prior edge-device campaigns where harvested VPN credentials became the initial access commodity for ransomware operators.

cyber_news.title: Windows Server 2016 reaches end of support in January — plan client migrations now
cyber_news.summary: Microsoft has confirmed Windows Server 2016 reaches end of support in January, after which no security updates will be released. Organizations running 2016 workloads need to inventory affected servers and complete upgrades or migrations before the deadline.
cyber_news.expanded: After the January cutoff, Windows Server 2016 systems stop receiving security patches entirely, meaning any vulnerability disclosed after that date becomes a permanent, unpatchable exposure on those hosts. The risk is compounded by the large number of 2016 servers still running internet-reachable roles such as IIS, RDS, and file services, and by the fact that Extended Security Updates are not indefinitely available for all licensing scenarios. Because in-place upgrade paths from 2016 to newer Windows Server releases have specific licensing and application-compatibility constraints, migration planning typically requires application inventory, dependency mapping, and staged workload moves that take months, not weeks.

cyber_news.title: Meta fined $25 billion over 43 million privacy violations with Cambridge Analytica lineage
cyber_news.summary: Meta has been hit with a $25 billion fine covering 43 million privacy violations tied to illegal user data sharing, with roots tracing back to the Cambridge Analytica scandal. The ruling is one of the largest privacy penalties ever imposed on a single company.
cyber_news.expanded: The penalty aggregates violations affecting 43 million users whose data was shared without lawful consent, with the court drawing a direct lineage to the original Cambridge Analytica data-sharing practices. The size of the fine reflects per-violation statutory damages rather than a single lump assessment, a structure that materially changes the financial risk calculus for large platforms handling consumer data at scale. The ruling also establishes precedent on how historical data-sharing practices can be re-litigated under newer privacy statutes, which is significant for any organization holding legacy consent records that predate modern privacy laws.

cyber_news.title: Ransomware affiliates (INC, The Gentlemen) ran AI-agent 'Phantom' autonomous red-team kill chain
cyber_news.summary: Exposed threat infrastructure has revealed that ransomware affiliates including INC Ransomware and The Gentlemen operated an AI agent dubbed 'Phantom' that autonomously executed full intrusion kill chains. The finding marks one of the first confirmed uses of agentic AI in real-world ransomware operations.
cyber_news.expanded: Analysis of the exposed infrastructure shows the 'Phantom' AI agent executing end-to-end intrusion tasks autonomously: reconnaissance of target networks, identification of exploitable entry points, credential abuse, and staging of ransomware deployment, effectively an automated red-team pipeline operated by criminal affiliates. The tooling was shared across affiliates of both INC Ransomware and The Gentlemen, indicating the agentic capability is circulating as rented or shared criminal infrastructure rather than being exclusive to one group. The significance is operational tempo: agentic execution compresses the traditional days-long intrusion timeline into hours, leaving far smaller windows for detection and response between initial access and ransomware detonation.

cyber_news.title: Two CVSS 9.0 Linux KSMBD pre-auth RCE flaws disclosed publicly before kernel fixes exist
cyber_news.summary: Two CVSS 9.0 pre-authentication remote code execution flaws in the Linux kernel's KSMBD SMB server have been disclosed publicly ahead of available kernel fixes. Any internet-exposed system running KSMBD is critically exposed until patches land upstream.
cyber_news.expanded: The flaws (tracked via ZDI-CAN-33774 among others) reside in the kernel-based SMB server (KSMBD) and are reachable before authentication completes, meaning an unauthenticated remote attacker can trigger memory corruption and achieve code execution in kernel context on exposed servers. The disclosure was published through zero-day initiative channels before upstream kernel fixes were merged, creating an unusual zero-patch window where the technical details are public but no remediation exists. KSMBD is not enabled in default kernel configurations, which limits the exposed population, but any deployment that enabled the in-kernel SMB server for file sharing, particularly internet-facing Linux hosts, is fully exposed in the interim.

cyber_news.title: GitLab critical patch fixes unauthenticated RCE (CVE-2026-110264); Ruby fixed underlying Onigmo regex bugs behind 4 critical GitLab RCEs
cyber_news.summary: GitLab has shipped a critical patch for CVE-2026-110264, an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw in self-hosted GitLab CE/EE. Separately, Ruby fixed three Onigmo regex engine bugs that were the root cause of four critical GitLab RCE vulnerabilities.
cyber_news.expanded: CVE-2026-110264 stems from an integer overflow triggered during regex compilation, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to corrupt memory and achieve code execution on the GitLab application server without any valid session. The deeper story is the shared root cause: the underlying Onigmo regex engine bugs in Ruby were responsible for four separate critical GitLab RCEs, meaning GitLab instances remained exposed through multiple CVE entries until both the GitLab application patches and the Ruby-level fixes were applied. Self-hosted GitLab CE/EE instances are externally reachable by design, and unauthenticated RCE on a code-hosting platform grants attackers direct access to source repositories, CI/CD pipelines, and deployment credentials.

cyber_news.title: HPE patches 72 ArubaOS flaws including eight max-severity auth-bypass and RCE issues
cyber_news.summary: HPE has released fixes for 72 vulnerabilities in ArubaOS, eight of which carry maximum severity ratings covering authentication bypass and remote code execution. The flaws affect Aruba mobility controllers, gateways, and APs that are commonly internet-reachable at network edges.
cyber_news.expanded: The eight max-severity issues span unauthenticated authentication bypass and remote code execution paths in ArubaOS, the operating system powering HPE Aruba mobility controllers, campus gateways, and access points. Several of the flaws are reachable through the management and PAPI (Aruba's access point management protocol) surfaces that are frequently exposed to the internet on edge deployments, allowing unauthenticated attackers to execute code with high privileges on the appliance. Because these devices sit at the network perimeter and handle all transit traffic, code execution on a controller effectively grants an attacker a tap and control point over the entire wireless and branch infrastructure behind it.

cyber_news.title: Critical Pillow flaw (CVE-2026-112900): crafted EPS image filename passed to Ghostscript enables command execution
cyber_news.summary: A critical flaw in Python's widely used Pillow image library allows command execution when a crafted EPS image with a malicious filename is processed and passed to Ghostscript. Any web service that processes user-uploaded images with Pillow is externally reachable.
cyber_news.expanded: The vulnerability (CVE-2026-112900) arises because Pillow delegates EPS file handling to Ghostscript and passes the input filename through to the interpreter without sufficient sanitization. By embedding shell metacharacters in the crafted EPS image's filename, an attacker can break out of the intended Ghostscript invocation and execute arbitrary operating system commands with the privileges of the image-processing service. The attack surface is broad: any web application that accepts user image uploads and runs them through Pillow for resizing, conversion, or validation can be driven to the vulnerable code path, and the filename is frequently attacker-controlled in upload pipelines, making this a practical pre-authentication RCE vector against image-handling backends.

cyber_news.title: Researchers remotely disabled abandoned Time4Popcorn updater (2M+ devices) that could have powered a botnet
cyber_news.summary: Researchers remotely disabled the abandoned Time4Popcorn (Popcorn Time) auto-updater still running on more than two million devices, closing a mass-RCE window before it could be abused. The dormant update mechanism could have been repurposed to push malware to the entire installed base.
cyber_news.expanded: The abandoned Time4Popcorn application shipped with an auto-update mechanism that continued phoning home on over two million devices long after the project died, and the update infrastructure had lapsed into a state where its control could effectively be reclaimed. Had a malicious actor taken over the update path, they would have inherited a ready-made distribution channel capable of pushing arbitrary code to the full installed base, a botnet-in-waiting comparable to historical updater hijacks. The researchers executed a coordinated takedown that remotely disabled the updater across the fleet, a rare proactive defensive operation that neutralized a mass-RCE capability in abandoned consumer software before criminal actors found it.

deep_dive.title: PHP2Shell: Critical PHP RCE vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) actively exploited in the wild
deep_dive.content: PHP2Shell refers to two critical remote code execution flaws in PHP's CGI handling (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) that are under mass exploitation against internet-exposed PHP/CGI web servers. Amazon reported detecting exploitation attempts four days before patches were released, indicating actors were probing the weakness ahead of public disclosure, and Mirai botnet operators have since joined the attacks with working ASLR-bypass exploits. CrowdStrike's analysis suggests weaponization obstacles, including non-default configuration requirements and memory-layout constraints, likely constrain reliable exploitation, but the volume of attempts and public PoCs are driving opportunistic scanning at scale. Emergency patches shipped for affected PHP versions, yet a further unpatched RCE (CVE-2026-115560) disclosed two days later extends the exposure window. Detection guidance centers on anomalous CGI request patterns and lol-php style execution traces, and the episode has drawn sharp criticism of the coordinated vulnerability disclosure process that let exploitation precede patch availability.

biggest_hacks.title: Capcom confirms CAPCOM ID breach exposing 11.7 million customer email addresses
biggest_hacks.summary: Capcom confirmed a breach of its CAPCOM ID system exposing the email addresses of 11.7 million customer accounts.

biggest_hacks.title: Quest Diagnostics confirms breach of Quanum Lab Services Manager exposed patient records
biggest_hacks.summary: Quest Diagnostics confirmed that a breach of its Quanum Lab Services Manager platform exposed certain patient records, triggering healthcare breach notification procedures.

biggest_hacks.title: Railway (PaaS) warns intruder may have accessed customer environment variables — all users urged to rotate secrets
biggest_hacks.summary: Platform-as-a-service provider Railway warned that an intruder may have accessed customer environment variables, and urged all users to rotate every secret stored in the platform.

biggest_hacks.title: State Bank of India suffers customer PII leak via underground market trading
biggest_hacks.summary: Customer PII from the State Bank of India was found being traded on underground markets, exposing affected customers to fraud and identity-theft risk.
